About

RISE is a youth banking concept for South Africans in their first months of earning, built around one question: will I still be okay after payday?

01
CHAPTER 01 OF 08

Problem

Getting a first job doesn’t end financial pressure. It changes its shape.

The problem

Payday arrives, family obligations take a fixed share, and little buffer remains. Banks show what happened, not what happens next, and shame stops people asking for help.

The solution

A buffer-first app: safe-to-spend, a predictive warning before the buffer breaks, and a judgment-free way to ask money questions.

HOW MIGHT WEprotect a first-job earner’s breathing room between paydays, without shame or jargon?
Why it mattersYouth unemployment climbed from 36.9% (2015) to 47.4% (Q2 2026). This study looks at the other side of that number: the first few months of being paid.

CHAPTER 02 OF 08

Research method & thinking

Three independent signals, three different explanations, one conclusion: this looks structural, not a mindset problem.

Emotional state

of under-35s report financial anxiety or stress, up 18% year on year.

Debt Rescue Money Stress Tracker, 2026

Skills gap

feel confident in their own digital financial skills.

SA Social Media Landscape report

Outlook

don’t know how to build a stable financial future.

Old Mutual Youth Generational Wealth Survey
Why theseIf young people were simply “bad with money”, one signal would be weak and the others fine. All three came back low.
LimitSkills and outlook are self-reported. Income and cost-of-living data would strengthen the case, and family remittance needs validating in interviews.
03
CHAPTER 03 OF 08

Synthesis & insights

Thabo doesn’t need a feature-rich banking app. He needs to know he’ll still be okay.

Thabo Mahlangu

The Cautious Provider
23JohannesburgFirst jobR6,800/month“If I spend this now, will I still be okay later?”
Core needFinancial breathing room: keeping his buffer above zero.
FrustrationsBanks show what happened, not what happens next. Jargon makes him feel judged. Surprise deductions break his sense of control.
BehaviourSplits money into transport, home, food and “do not touch”. Prefers reversible moves over locked commitments.
The insight: a monthly loop, with one designable point
1Payday arrives
2Familyremittance claims a fixed share
3Little bufferor none remains
4Shameblocks help-seeking
RISE intervenes here
5No habitor safety net forms
Why a loopA linear journey can’t explain why the problem returns every month. RISE can’t change family expectations or payroll dates, but it can make checking in private and judgment-free.
So whatPrioritise safe-to-spend, upcoming deductions and buffer warnings. Design for pressure moments, not account management.

Persona and quotes are an illustrative composite built from secondary research.

CHAPTER 05 OF 08

Design direction

Calm, shame-free, and built for pressure moments.

⚡Design for pressureWarn and guide when money is tight.
🛡️Protect before you growSeparate stability money from ambition money.
💬Ask without shameSuggested prompts, no blank screens.
🎨Colour carries meaningBlue action, orange obligation, red risk, green progress.
From sketch to screen
Why sketch firstThree screens carried the whole idea: home, warning, Ask RISE. I settled them on paper before touching UI.
06
CHAPTER 06 OF 08

Solution & design decisions

Five decisions, each replacing a banking convention.

BarrierConvention rejectedRISE decision
Falling below zeroBuffer as one more savings goalBuffer as a first-class object
Shame blocks helpFAQ or hidden chatbotAsk RISE with suggested prompts
JargonLiteracy hub of articlesMoney 101 micro-lessons
Income ≠ life stageKYC-first onboardingContext-first onboarding
Alerts come too lateFixed low-balance alertPredictive buffer warning
Decision 1

Make the Buffer a first-class object

DecisionSurface the Buffer as protected money, front and centre on Home.
WhyThabo’s progress isn’t wealth yet. It’s surviving the month with something left.
RejectedA buffer beside a phone or holiday goal. It would make a safety net compete with aspirations.
Home: R214 safe to spend
Decision 2 & 3

Ask RISE and Money 101, not a ticket and a glossary

DecisionA clear place to ask, with suggested prompts, plus short lessons beside everyday banking.
WhyEmbarrassment stops people asking (loop point 4). Education works best near the moment of uncertainty.
RejectedAn FAQ, a hidden chatbot, a literacy hub of definitions.
Ask RISE · Learn
Decision 4

Start with context, not compliance

DecisionLight questions on life stage, income and habits replace one dense KYC screen. A R500 safety cushion is set before the dashboard.
WhyA new hire, someone on probation and someone months in may earn the same but need different support.
RejectedKYC-first. It tells the bank who the customer is, not what they’re navigating.
Where are you now? · Safety cushion
Decision 5

Warn before the buffer breaks

DecisionWhen an action is likely to dent the buffer, show today’s balance against the projected one and three ways to protect it.
WhyIt turns an alert into a decision-support moment using Thabo’s own context.
RejectedA fixed-threshold alert that reacts too late and ignores upcoming obligations.
Heads up: R320 projected by 21 Sep

CHAPTER 07 OF 08

Success & impact

Success is a safety net that survives the month, not an account that gets opened.

Buffer > R0Primary measure: did the net survive the month?
SecondaryApp opens on payday. Shows habit forming, not that anyone is better off.
RejectedSign-up rate. Easy to inflate with a marketing push.
IntendedMoney left over · fewer surprises · help sought sooner.
NORTH STARDoes Thabo still have something in his Buffer the day before his next payslip lands?

Not built or shipped, so there are no usage results yet. These measures define what impact would look like.

08
CHAPTER 08 OF 08

Lessons & next steps

Name the loop first

Seeing the monthly loop showed me the one point a product could change.

Reject on purpose

Naming what each decision replaces made the trade-offs easy to defend.

Be honest about evidence

Secondary research and a composite persona are a start, so I said so and planned the test.

Next steps
Test with real first-job earnersDo the Buffer, warning and Ask RISE behave outside a prototype?
Stress-test irregular incomeGig and informal pay must hold when payday moves.
Measure what mattersIs something left in the Buffer the day before payslip?

Thank you for reading my case study.
